## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Hirijātaka* (Ja 363) is a birth story preserved in the *Jātaka* collection of the Pali Canon. Set at Jetavana, the narrative was delivered by the Buddha regarding a wealthy merchant from a border province who was a friend of Anāthapiṇḍika. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta was born as a merchant of Benares (*Bārāṇasiseṭṭhi*) [Fausböll 1883]. When foreign merchants were deprived of their property and forced into flight because they had neglected hospitality toward visiting strangers, the merchant of Benares recited verses emphasizing the virtue of integrity, advising that one should remain true in deed to every promise and avoid unfulfillable boasts [Sarada Thero, Treasury of Truth].

  Additionally, DharmaNexus identifies machine alignments with the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001-2) and the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* translations (T 99 and T 100) [DharmaNexus].
